Subject: HelixAI DPA — proposed redlines and carveouts (analytics subprocessors)

Hi Grace / Olga,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Helix is excited about the integration with Redwood. Our legal team attached a set of proposed redlines to the standard DPA focused on analytic exports and telemetry retention. The key asks are:

- Allow Helix to retain aggregated telemetry for 36 months for product usage analytics (aggregated, no PII).
- Permit a named analytics subprocessor (NimbusMetrics) for downstream reporting.
- Explicitly exclude model training from any customer-provided runtime traces.

We appreciate that some of these touch product telemetry and security policy. Can your team provide a short evaluator matrix mapping each redline to: product impact, security risk level, and proposed mitigation? Ideally we can get that by EOD Wednesday so our procurement team can confirm timelines.

Attached: Helix-DPA-Proposed-Redlines.pdf

Note any engineering work and rough ETA.

Thanks Grace — quick notes inline and attached a short comment export (olga_comments.txt). High level:

- Telemetry retention 36 months (aggregated): security impact medium. Aggregation reduces PII risk but retention window is outside our default 12-month retention for aggregated telemetry. Mitigation: require Helix to sign an addendum limiting use to product analytics and prohibiting re-identification; enforce encryption at rest and access controls. Product implications: we will need a schema flag to mark "customer-long-retention" events so downstream ETL can route to a longer-lived storage tier (roughly 2-3 engineer-weeks).

- Named subprocessor (NimbusMetrics): not on allowlist. Karthik will need SOC2 Type II + DPA and an architecture diagram for data flows. If Nimbus processes telemetry only (no PII), risk is lower but still must be reviewed.

- "No-training" clause for runtime traces: technically we can promise that we do not use runtime traces for model training, but we need a contractual mechanism to exclude traces from any research datasets and to restrict internal access. That requires an internal policy update plus a short audit trail; estimate 1 week of small policy and audit work plus tooling to mark these traces as "no-train" in storage.

Next steps I recommend: populate the matrix with the dispositions below. I attached my exported comments and a proposed mitigation column in the template.

Attached: olga_comments.txt

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Product Security Engineer
